items.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021
items.q: And John Gilmore was very sweet and soft spoken

ctx.x: Well I used to go and visit there, Monk. I used to visit the place. This is as thrilling as it gets. When I went to Sun Ra’s and the first time I went and he said, “Hello, Jerry.” That was it. I had arrived. He knew my name. And he was talking to, I remember very clearly he was talking to an Italian video producer, you know, from Italy, who was trying to

make a deal with Sun Ra for some kind of video or something. I guess Sun Ra wanted to get off the phone with him and he said, “I’m talking to Jerry. I have to go.” That was thrilling to me. So I have wonderful memories of visiting Sun Ra’s place and, you know, meeting some of the band there. And there was crazy artwork there, artwork that listeners had sent him or that followers of the band, friends, whatever, had sent him. And the place was what Sun Ra’s place you might expect it to look like. It was very cool.…

You transitioned to starting a record label and I’m wondering if the change in the music scene caused that to happen somewhat. I read something about the distribution of CDs and so forth. Did it make your — was there a time when your record store became untenable?
